question: Do those congenitally deaf also attain clear cognition of things?
premises: Those congenitally deaf apprehend aspects of things through form, touch, and other senses.
For them, cognition is never entirely unknown in any respect.
inference: Clear cognition of objects is available through non-auditory senses as well.
uncertainties: jātijaḍā is read as congenitally deaf or congenitally dull; the sensory examples favor deaf.
plain_english: Thus those congenitally deaf apprehend an aspect of things clearly through form, touch, and so on; for them cognition is never unknown anywhere.
